claim_under_review: For every integer \(n\ge4\) and \(2\le k\le n-2\), let \(P_{n,k}=\{x\in[0,1]^n:\sum_i x_i=k\}\), and let \(Q_{H,J}\) be the convex hull of all its vertices except two distinct support indicators \(\mathbf1_H,\mathbf1_J\), with \(|H|=|J|=k\). Its normalized volume satisfies \(\mathcal V(Q_{H,J})=A(n-1,k-1)-2\binom{n-2}{k-1}+\mathbf1_{\{|H\cap J|=k-1\}}\), where \(\mathcal V=(n-1)!\operatorname{vol}_{n-1}/\sqrt n\) and \(A\) is the Eulerian number. The strict removed vertex caps have disjoint interiors unless \(|H\cap J|=k-1\), in which case their intersection closure is one full-dimensional unimodular simplex of normalized volume one. In every case \(d_H(P_{n,k},Q_{H,J})=\sqrt{n/[k(n-k)]}\), and precisely the two removed vertices attain the Hausdorff distance. The additive nonadjacent volume formula and nonadjacent metric case are recognized prior results for sparse-paving matroids; the claimed new structural content is the adjacent, nonmatroid overlap simplex, its exact one-unit interaction, and the extension of the metric plateau to adjacent deletions.

correctness.rationale: The two-step vertex-cut argument rules out nonoriginal fractional vertices even for an adjacent pair by analyzing the product-of-simplices facet. Two cap volumes follow from a pyramid calculation, while the adjacent intersection is an integrally invertible standard (n−1)-simplex, so its normalized volume is one; nonadjacent cap interiors are disjoint. Inclusion–exclusion proves the exact all-rank formula. Each removed vertex has an explicit feasible orthogonal foot simultaneously satisfying both cuts, giving identical sharp Hausdorff distance, and convexity with distinct residuals proves only the removed vertices are deepest. Direct hull tests passed 37 rank/overlap orbit profiles and exact integer determinants passed 28 profiles. Tests are finite only; analytical proof establishes the unbounded quantifiers.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Lam–Postnikov Theorem 3.2 offers a general lattice-point sum for alcoved polytopes including suitable reordered two-cut hypersimplices; it is acknowledged as broad algorithmic coverage of volume. Ferroni–Schröter and the sparse-paving projection theorem imply the entire nonadjacent pair case. Neither asserts the adjacent nonmatroid cap intersection is exactly one unimodular simplex or combines that overlap with unchanged Hausdorff depth; this structural geometric clause, not the mere applicability of a general volume algorithm, is the originality claim.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is a full-rank, two-erasure geometric classification with one unimodular cap-overlap simplex exactly for adjacent (nonmatroid) missing bases and unchanged Euclidean damage. The best prior sparse-paving theorems already cover nonadjacent erasures; these are explicitly acknowledged, not claimed as discoveries. Lam–Postnikov provides a general alcoved volume enumeration but does not state the local overlap-simplex geometry or the adjacent-case metric plateau. No exact equivalent was found in checked full texts or targeted record searches; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete all-rank classification of two-vertex damage in hypersimplices, motivated by the recently classified extremal Johnson simplex-edge configurations. The nonmatroid adjacent pair has a full-dimensional unimodular overlap region rather than the disjoint-volume geometry of sparse-paving matroid erasures, yielding exactly one unit of interaction; surprisingly the sharp Euclidean worst-case error does not change between orbit types. The simplex geometry, sharp equality cases and volume-versus-metric separation supply a reusable structural benchmark rather than an arbitrary low-dimensional table or trivial parameter substitution.
